title: Rectangular bar
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Draw the first two-dimensional sketch on the first face, forming the first loop with four lines. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.0938, 0.0). The second line starts at (0.0938, 0.0) and ends at (0.0938, 0.75). The third line starts at (0.0938, 0.75) and ends at (0.0, 0.75). The fourth line completes the loop by starting at (0.0, 0.75) and ending at the origin (0.0, 0.0). Scale the entire sketch by a factor of 0.75. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero and translating it with a vector also set to zero. Extrude the transformed sketch 0.0375 units along the normal direction to create a new solid body. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. The final dimensions of the rectangular bar are a length of 0.09375 units, a width of 0.75 units, and a height of 0.0375 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.0938, 0).lineTo(0.0938, 0.75).lineTo(0, 0.75).close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the rectangular bar
r = sketch.extrude(0.0375)

# Optionally, you can round the edges if needed
# r = r.edges().fillet(0.01)  # Uncomment this line to round the edges

import cadquery as cq

# Define the sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.0938, 0).lineTo(0.0938, 0.75).lineTo(0, 0.75).close()

# Extrude the sketch
extrusion = sketch.extrude(0.0375)

# Apply the sketch scale (if needed)
# Note: The sketch scale is applied to the sketch before extrusion, but in this case, it's 0.75 which is the same as the width.
# So, we don't need to apply any additional scaling.

# The final model
r = extrusion
